passages.title: Naming and praising the Lord of all worlds
passages.why: These four ayat form one unbroken act of divine self-disclosure — the Name invoked, praise assigned to the Lord of all worlds, and His mercy and sovereignty over the Day of Judgment named as the grounds for that praise — closing at 4 because the qudsi division of the sūrah places everything through 'Master of the Day of Judgment' as Allah's own portion.

passages.title: The servant's pledge and plea for guidance
passages.why: From ayah 5 the voice turns from describing Allah to addressing Him, and the exclusive pledge of worship and reliance flows directly into the single petition it authorizes — guidance along the Straight Path, defined in ayah 7 by the company who walked it and the two who strayed from it — so the run cannot be cut without severing the request from its qualification.
